pathway.title: Millrose Properties, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Revenue is contractual and well covered, but it depends on one builder group and on a contractual pause right. Option fees were 99.28% of third-quarter revenue, and the 2025 annual report schedules about USD 3.1 billion of undiscounted option fees on homesites then under contract. Lennar paid USD 144.9 million, 69% of the quarter's revenue, and may pause takedown and construction deadlines for up to six months in each of two periods, cutting its monthly option payments to half the applicable rate, if a local home price index falls 10% or more, in a public health emergency or at its own election. Its share has fallen from 84% in FY2025 as 21 other counterparties were added, and management says about 42% of the asset base is outside the Lennar program once the Dream Finders funding is counted. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C13; calculation C17; 10-K_2024-12-31_d931976d10k.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 258; 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 33–35, 51, 160, 174; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3

Margins are not the weak point, but the cost base does not shrink when income does. Reported EBITDA margin was 85.18% over the last twelve months because the company has no employees and its main operating cost is a management fee of 1.25% of Tangible Assets, about USD 30.3 million or 14.34% of third-quarter revenue. The fee follows assets, not income, so a fall in option income would pass almost wholly to EBITDA, and interest is the larger fixed claim: third-quarter EBITDA covered accrued interest expense 3.83x, against 4.18x over the last twelve months. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 35

Cash generation is a recycling of capital, and growth and distributions depend on borrowing. Takedowns of homesites were 85.86% of operating cash flow in the nine months to September 30, 2026. Without them operating cash flow was about USD 362 million, below dividends paid of about USD 379 million, so net borrowing of about USD 1.2 billion financed investment in new homesites and the distribution. The model recycles its own capital while takedowns continue; it does not generate free cash flow after distributions. Basis: calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

Leverage and coverage have deteriorated faster than the annual picture shows. Total debt to EBITDA rose from 3.83x at June 30, 2026 to 4.95x at September 30, 2026, and debt to capitalization of 36.33% is about USD 456 million of debt above management's 33% maximum target on the equity then reported. Net debt to EBITDA of 4.85x was 6.18x pro forma for the Dream Finders closing on October 20, 2026 and 5.04x pro forma for the dividend paid on October 15, 2026, each taken alone; the effect of the October 6, 2026 notes is not established. Cash interest cover of 4.66x is the first reading with a full year of coupons, and the annual coupons on the four senior note issues outstanding after October 6, 2026, about USD 193 million, are covered 3.50x by last-twelve-months EBITDA before any floating-rate interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 29, 40–41

Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months on contractual maturities, but it is thinner and its headroom is unverified. Cash plus undrawn committed facilities fell by about USD 545 million in the third quarter to about USD 0.8 billion, and only the revolving facility's USD 750 million is a working buffer, whose availability depends on a borrowing base the filings do not print, while the delayed draw term loan, almost fully drawn, can be drawn only until March 2027. Maturities before 2028 are small, but 70.51% of September 30, 2026 principal falls due in 2030, and covenant levels are not printed anywhere, so compliance is known only as reported. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34

Financial policy favors shareholders while leverage is above the stated target. Dividends paid were 99.94% of net income in the nine months, the quarterly dividend has risen to USD 0.79 a share, and on October 26, 2026 the board authorized repurchases of up to USD 250 million with none stated. The 33% maximum was stated in the first-quarter release and not restated in the later releases, so whether it still binds management is not established. The only contractual limit with a stated level is Lennar's ceiling of one times equity on debt, with debt to equity at 0.57x, and the August 27, 2026 amendment to Lennar's rights is not described. Basis: calculation C19; calculation C21; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 76

Growth is moving into exposures that sit outside the pooled option protection. Funding for Dream Finders totals about USD 1.1 billion, of which a preferred instrument paying a 12% dividend is USD 487.5 million at purchase cost, and single-family rental homes bought from Lennar cost about USD 333 million. Management states a 10.8% yield on other agreements against 8.5% on the Lennar program, but the preferred instrument is a perpetual equity security of Dream Finders that ranks behind its debt and that Dream Finders may redeem from the third anniversary, its covenants are not described, rental income is not yet reported, and how much of the capital held with other counterparties is pooled is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 26, 41, 43, 45, 47

Governance gives creditors little direct control, and a securities class action adds an unquantified cost. Class B stock held by the Miller Family carries about 43% of the votes, Lennar holds consent rights over the manager and over debt above one times equity, and the manager is paid on assets. A securities class action was filed on October 9, 2026 for purchasers from February 7, 2025 to October 2, 2026; the management fee does not cover extraordinary litigation, so any cost falls on Millrose, and management says the claims have no merit. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 35, 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75

runs.text: Contractual, pooled option income is the main credit support. Option fees were 99.28% of third-quarter revenue and are paid monthly on invested capital under agreements in which deposits are forfeited on non-exercise and options cross-terminate within a pool, and no option has been terminated since inception, so the cash that services debt has been predictable. The support is a design and a short record, not a tested downturn outcome. Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 25, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34

The cost base is thin, so income converts to cover. Reported EBITDA margin was 85.18% over the last twelve months because there are no employees and the manager is paid 1.25% of Tangible Assets, so each dollar of option income reaches interest cover with little leakage, although the fee follows assets and does not fall when income does. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C20

The funding stack is long and mostly unsecured, so refinancing risk is back-ended. About 92.71% of contractual principal at September 30, 2026 is unsecured, the senior notes carry fixed coupons, maturities before 2028 are only the purchase money mortgages, and the first large maturity is the rental facility in 2028, followed by the revolving and delayed draw facilities and the 2030 notes in 2030. That leaves little to refinance while takedowns continue. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 33–34

Counterparty diversification is improving. Lennar's share of revenue fell from 84% in FY2025 to 69% in the third quarter as capital held under other agreements rose to 36.46% of invested capital, which lowers dependence on a single payer and earns a higher stated yield of 10.8%. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 45

Builder deposits and takedown proceeds fund part of growth without new debt. Builder deposits were about USD 1.0 billion at September 30, 2026, up from December 31, 2025, and takedown proceeds were about USD 0.8 billion in the third quarter, so a share of new investment does not call on lenders. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

Leverage is above target and rising. Total debt to EBITDA of 4.95x and debt to capitalization of 36.33% follow a quarter in which debt grew by about USD 0.9 billion before the funded assets earned EBITDA, and net leverage of 6.18x pro forma for the Dream Finders closing on October 20, 2026 would be higher still, so the cushion for a revenue shock is smaller than at June 30, 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C15

One builder group and its pause right drive the income. Lennar paid 69% of third-quarter revenue and may pause for up to six months at half the option rate, so a market shock can cut income without any default, while pooled protection and the parent guarantee address default rather than a pause. Basis: calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 51

Financial policy leaves no retained cushion. Dividends were 99.94% of nine-month net income and a repurchase of up to USD 250 million is authorized while debt to capitalization exceeds the stated target, so equity returns compete with creditors for the same cash and growth is funded by borrowing. Basis: calculation C9; calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

Liquidity is thinner and its true headroom is unverified. Cash plus undrawn committed facilities fell to about USD 0.8 billion in a quarter, availability depends on borrowing bases that are not printed, and the covenants that would show headroom are named without levels. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33–34

Governance and exposure outside the pools weaken creditor control. An external manager paid on assets, Lennar and Miller Family control rights, a preferred instrument in one builder, rental homes with no earnings record and a securities class action all sit beside debt that ranks ahead of the preferred. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 35, 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 43, 75

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Millrose was created by Lennar's spin-off on February 7, 2025, which contributed about USD 5.5 billion of land assets and about USD 1.0 billion of cash that included USD 585 million of option deposit liabilities. Since then it has bought the Rausch homesites on February 10, 2025 for about USD 859 million net of deposits, funded USD 494.5 million at the June 25, 2025 closing of New Home's acquisition of Landsea, closed its first multifamily land banking acquisition with JPI on July 30, 2026, and supported Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes with funding of about USD 1.068 billion across September 14 and October 20, 2026. The FY2024 annual report gave about USD 876 million for the Rausch purchase, a difference logged in the conflict register. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2024-12-31_d931976d10k.htm.jsonl, page 216; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 43

New debt came in four steps. The company issued USD 1.25 billion of senior notes due 2030 on August 7, 2025 and USD 750 million due 2032 on September 11, 2025, replaced its secured revolving facility with an unsecured credit agreement on March 25, 2026, signed a limited-recourse rental facility of up to USD 235 million on September 30, 2026, and closed USD 1.0 billion of senior notes due 2029 and 2031 on October 6, 2026. Amounts and ratios are in Financial foundation. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24, 34, 40

fields.value: Financial foundation for Millrose Properties, Inc. (issuer mrp-2017206) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the supplied annual and quarterly filings and earnings releases through the quarter ended September 30, 2026: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and cover, in the issuer's reporting currency, US dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage rose sharply in the third quarter: total debt reached 4.95x last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 30, 2026, against 3.83x at June 30, 2026, which leaves creditors more exposed to a slowdown in homesite takedowns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt to total capitalization reached 36.33%, above the 33% maximum that management stated as its target in the first quarter, while cash interest cover of 4.66x is the first reading that carries a full year of senior note coupons. Liquidity fell to about USD 0.8 billion from about USD 1.4 billion at June 30, 2026. A further USD 1.0 billion of notes closed on October 6, 2026 and about USD 1.1 billion of Dream Finders funding followed; neither is in the September 30, 2026 figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third quarter drove the rise. Contractual principal increased by USD 860.022 million in three months: USD 150 million on the revolving facility, USD 496.875 million on the delayed draw term loan, which was undrawn until then, and USD 213.147 million on the new single-family rental facility. The money funded a USD 170.6 million preferred instrument for Dream Finders, 1,233 rental homes carried at USD 332.651 million and land and development spending. None of these earns EBITDA in the quarter it is funded: the rental homes are not yet depreciating or let, and preferred income of USD 0.996 million sits below operating income. Leverage therefore overshoots first and falls only if the new assets reach their yield, which creditors have to underwrite.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Against this, the growth rests on contractual cash flows. Management's own run rate of USD 221 million of quarterly income at September 30, 2026 compares with reported third-quarter revenue of USD 211.004 million, so about USD 10 million a quarter is contracted but not yet in revenue. The reading improves if fourth-quarter revenue reaches that run rate with debt flat and worsens if takedowns slow, because takedown proceeds fund both reinvestment and the repayment of revolving drawings (USD 1,148.125 million repaid in nine months).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover of 4.66x at September 30, 2026 compares with 7.58x at June 30, 2026 and 6.76x at March 31, 2026 because the window now holds all four semi-annual coupon dates of the 2030 and 2032 notes: cash interest paid in the last twelve months rose from USD 85.351 million to USD 144.864 million while EBITDA rose from USD 647.291 million to USD 674.906 million. The fiscal-year reading of 20.30x is not a trend point, since those notes were issued in August and September 2025 and paid no coupon in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest expense, which accrues, gives a lower and steadier cover: last-twelve-months EBITDA over interest expense of USD 161.542 million is 4.18x. Cover will fall further, because the annual coupons on the four senior note issues outstanding after October 6, 2026 total USD 192.8125 million, which alone is 3.50x covered by last-twelve-months EBITDA, before interest on the revolving, delayed draw and rental facilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net cash from operating activities was USD 2,558.409 million in the nine months to September 30, 2026, but USD 2,196.771 million of it, 85.86%, is takedowns of homesites net of builder deposit credits, which is capital coming back rather than earnings. Without it, operating cash flow was USD 361.638 million, close to net income of USD 378.767 million. Investing outflows of USD 3,369.202 million, of which USD 3,150.232 million was new homesite investment, exceeded operating cash flow by USD 810.793 million, and dividends paid of USD 378.522 million widened the gap. Net borrowing closed it: USD 2,170 million drawn less USD 1,148.125 million repaid, plus USD 213.147 million on the rental facility. The platform recycles its own capital, but debt funds the growth and the distribution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure is not reported in maintenance and growth categories; land and development spending is shown as investment in homesites under option contracts, so no capital-intensity ratio is calculated, and working-capital movements are small beside the takedown line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 64.535 million plus undrawn committed facilities of USD 774.978 million gives USD 839.513 million at September 30, 2026, down from USD 1,384.171 million at June 30, 2026. Only USD 3.125 million remains on the delayed draw term loan and USD 21.853 million on the rental facility, so the revolving facility's USD 750 million is the working buffer, and its availability depends on a borrowing base the filings do not print. Near-term claims on cash are the dividend of USD 131.178 million paid on October 15, 2026, purchase money mortgage principal of USD 4 million in the fourth quarter, the Dream Finders closing and future land development commitments of USD 6.7 billion, about 73% of them to Lennar, which Millrose funds as builders exercise options.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net proceeds of about USD 991.2 million from the October 6, 2026 notes rebuild liquidity, but the amount left after the Dream Finders funding and the revolver repayment is not printed, so liquidity after the quarter is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Builder deposits were USD 1,003.209 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 927.004 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of USD 76.205 million. They are non-interest-bearing money held from homebuilders against their option contracts and credited against takedown prices, so they fund part of the invested capital without being debt and lower the borrowing Millrose needs. The filings do not say what happens to them if Millrose failed to deliver finished homesites, which is not established. A separate non-debt obligation, the development guarantee holdback liability, is USD 100 million at every balance-sheet date and arose from the Rausch acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four financing events in 2026 shaped the balance sheet. On March 25, 2026 the company replaced its secured revolving facility with an unsecured credit agreement of a USD 1.335 billion revolving facility and a USD 500 million delayed draw term loan, releasing the liens; on August 5, 2026 an amendment cut every margin by 0.25 percentage points; on September 21, 2026 the accordion raised revolving commitments by USD 50 million to USD 1.385 billion; and on September 30, 2026 a limited-recourse rental facility of up to USD 235 million was signed, with USD 213.147 million outstanding at quarter end. The unsecured structure puts the new facilities pari passu with the senior notes, while the rental facility and the purchase money mortgages rank ahead of the notes against their own collateral. Events of default under the credit agreement include the external manager ceasing to act without a replacement acceptable to lenders within 90 days, which ties the lenders to the manager arrangement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure were searched for and are small or absent: no pension or retiree medical obligations, factoring or supplier finance, lease liabilities or consent decrees appear in the 2025 annual report or the third-quarter report, and no material litigation is reported. The claims that do sit outside debt are USD 13 million of seller notes in other liabilities, the USD 100 million development guarantee holdback, builder deposits of USD 1,003.209 million, the management fee of USD 30.264 million in the third quarter payable to the external manager, the dividend payable of USD 131.178 million and future land development commitments of USD 6.7 billion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four events after the balance-sheet date are kept out of period figures and shown with their dates in the post-balance-sheet table: the USD 1.0 billion senior notes of October 6, 2026, the dividend paid on October 15, 2026, the Dream Finders closing on October 20, 2026 and the share repurchase authority of up to USD 250 million approved on October 26, 2026, under which no repurchase is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dream Finders support carries three figures. The release headline of about USD 1.1 billion is management's total; the quarterly report states aggregate funding of about USD 1.068 billion, of which USD 170.6 million was funded on September 14, 2026 and is already in the balance sheet; the sum of USD 170.6 million, USD 316.9 million and about USD 580 million is USD 1,067.5 million. Only the USD 896.9 million funded after quarter end is a post-balance-sheet event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four definitions need care. Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states none. Management's total corporate debt of USD 3.1 billion leaves out the limited-recourse rental facility, whereas the ratio of 36% it states matches debt including that facility. The 33% debt-to-capitalization maximum stated in the first-quarter release and the 2025 annual report is not restated in the later releases while the ratio has passed it. The purchase money mortgage repayment schedule changed between the second- and third-quarter reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three period limits apply. FY2025 includes the pre-spin period to February 7, 2025 and pre-spin expenses of USD 24.96 million, FY2024 is a carve-out with no revenue and is not carried into the tables, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is calculated as the year less nine months because no fourth-quarter statement was reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every amount is in US dollars; the statements are in thousands and the money tables in millions. Each result is worked from the inputs shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maximum leverage ratio, minimum interest coverage ratio and minimum tangible net worth tests of the credit agreement are named but no level, step-down or reported ratio is printed in any of the eight documents, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated and nothing is inferred. Severity: High. Action: Supply the executed credit agreement or the compliance certificate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated as income from operations, with no depreciation or amortization of operating assets presented; any covenant EBITDA may differ. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain management's covenant definition of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Amounts drawn on the delayed draw term loan and repaid on the revolving facility after September 30, 2026 are not printed, so pro forma net debt after the October 6, 2026 notes is not stated; the Dream Finders and dividend rows are isolated effects. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the October 2026 current reports and the borrowing position at the latest date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Borrowing-base calculations for the revolving, delayed draw and rental facilities are not printed, so undrawn commitments may exceed what can be borrowed; no letters of credit are disclosed in any document (searched letters of credit, standby, LC). Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the borrowing base certificate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The purchase money mortgage schedule differs: USD 29 million due in 2026 and USD 4 million in 2027 in the 2025 annual report and the first two quarterly reports, against USD 4 million in the fourth quarter of 2026 and USD 29 million in 2027 in the latest report; the latest is used and the balance of USD 33 million is the same. Severity: Low. Action: Confirm with the mortgage terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - FY2024 and FY2023 statements are of the pre-spin predecessor with no revenue and are not carried into the period tables, so growth from FY2024 and year-on-year comparisons across the spin cannot be measured; FY2025 includes the period to February 7, 2025. Severity: Medium. Action: Compare from FY2025 only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fourth quarter of 2025 is not reported as an income statement and is calculated as FY2025 less nine months 2025; no separate 2025 quarterly reports are supplied, so the 2025 stubs come from comparatives in the 2026 reports. Severity: Low. Action: Supply the fourth-quarter 2025 release and the 2025 quarterly reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Dashes in the statements are carried as not supplied rather than zero: the provision line in Q1 2026 and Q3 2026, pre-spin expenses and the pre-spin adjustment in every 2026 column, and the opening cash balance for FY2025; the lines for preferred instruments, rental properties and the rental facility are not presented before the third quarter of 2026. Severity: Low. Action: None needed; the lines are stated in the filings as nil or absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost of sales, gross profit, depreciation and amortization, and maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not presented, so those lines and ratios are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: None; the business model has no cost of sales line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Carrying value is disclosed in aggregate only, net of issuance costs, so the instrument table carries principal and one financing cost adjustment; the 2029 and 2031 notes are outside the September 30, 2026 table. Severity: Low. Action: Supply instrument-level carrying values if needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue is not split by segment because there is one reportable segment; the Lennar share of revenues is stated for FY2025, the second and third quarters and nine months but not for the first quarter of 2026. Severity: Low. Action: None needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid lags interest expense because the first coupons on the 2030 and 2032 notes were paid in 2026, so cash interest cover for FY2025 and the earlier 2026 quarters overstates the position; interest expense cover is given beside it. Severity: Medium. Action: Read cover at September 30, 2026 and after.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 33% maximum debt-to-capitalization target is stated in the first-quarter release and the 2025 annual report but not in the second- and third-quarter releases, and the stated ratio of 36% exceeds it; the filings do not say whether the target still applies or how it is defined. Severity: Medium. Action: Ask management whether the target stands and on which debt definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Option fee revenue is recognized on an effective-interest basis for sales-type leases and its relation to cash option payments is not reconciled in the sources read, so no cash revenue figure is stated. Severity: Low. Action: Supply the cash option payments received by quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of Millrose Properties, Inc. (issuer mrp-2017206) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and related-party arrangements, capital allocation and dated history through the supplied filings and releases to the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Millrose's cash flows are contractual and well pooled, but concentration in Lennar and governance rights held outside creditor control limit the protection, so creditors should treat counterparty and governance risk as the main drivers of credit quality.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lennar supplied 69% of third-quarter revenue and 63.54% of invested capital; its payment obligations are capped at USD 50 million per pool for spin-off assets and USD 25 million per pool for later assets, and a Lennar Corporation guarantee backs them. One family holds 98.7% of Class B stock and about 43% of the votes, Lennar keeps consent rights over the manager and over debt above one times equity, and a securities class action was filed on October 9, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is good but rests on one counterparty group. Lennar supplied 69% of third-quarter revenue and 71% of nine-month revenue, down from 84% in FY2025, because other counterparties now hold 36.46% of invested capital at a weighted yield of 10.8% against 8.5% on the Lennar program. Option fees are paid monthly on invested capital, so the cash that services the notes depends on option payments and takedowns from Lennar's divisions, and the caps of USD 50 million and USD 25 million per pool bound what Lennar owes if it walks from a pool whose average invested capital is USD 121.65 million. Protection after a Lennar default would therefore come mainly from resale of the land and the Lennar Corporation guarantee, not from the payment caps.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contractual protection is strong in design and untested in practice. 93% of invested capital is pooled so that one counterparty's option termination can put the rest of its pool at risk, deposits are non-refundable, counterparties bear cost overruns and development obligations, and the filings report zero option terminations since inception. That record has been earned in a period without a recorded counterparty delinquency or default, so pooling, forfeiture and resale have not been exercised against a stressed builder, and the evidence supports the design rather than the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is moving into credit-like exposures that sit outside the pool protections. The Dream Finders support totals about USD 1.1 billion, of which a preferred instrument paying a 12% dividend is USD 487.5 million at purchase cost and the rest is homesites under option agreements; development loans, reduced by a USD 284.2 million payoff, and single-family rental homes bought from Lennar for about USD 333 million add loan and operating exposure, with more homes agreed for USD 150.3 million. A preferred instrument is equity-like and ranks behind the issuer's debt, and its covenants and ranking are not described, so the preferred capital depends on one builder's post-merger performance rather than on pooled land.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance gives creditors little direct control and leaves decisions with a manager paid on assets. Millrose has no employees; the external manager earns 1.25% of Tangible Assets a year, which was USD 30.3 million in the third quarter, or 14.34% of revenue, so its pay rises with balance-sheet growth whether the growth is funded by debt or equity. Extraordinary litigation costs fall outside the fee and are borne by Millrose, opportunities are shared with Kennedy Lewis vehicles by rotation, and the July 2026 multifamily facility was set up by the manager's parent. Replacing it without cause during the initial term would cost 2.5 times the average annual fee, about USD 219.38 million on the FY2025 fee. Lenders hold one lever: the credit agreement defaults if the manager ceases to act and no replacement acceptable to lenders is appointed within 90 days, and the manager can itself leave on 60 days' notice after an uncured default.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control rights held by Lennar and the Miller Family constrain the board in ways that can protect or hinder creditors. Class B stock held by the Miller Family carries about 43% of the votes and has a separate class vote on mergers and Class B issuance, and Lennar's rights include a ceiling of one times debt to equity (0.57x at September 30, 2026), consent over secured financing that mixes Lennar and other assets, and consent over a replacement manager until the sunset threshold, which Lennar's contributed assets falling below 10% of total assets for six consecutive months would trigger. The ceiling protects unsecured creditors from leverage above one times equity, but the August 27, 2026 amendment to these rights is not described, so whether each right still binds is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation favors shareholders while leverage sits above the stated target. Cash dividends paid in the nine months to September 30, 2026 were 99.94% of net income and 97.81% of AFFO, the dividend rose in each quarter to USD 0.79 a share, and the board authorized a USD 250 million buyback on October 26, 2026 with no repurchase stated. The third-quarter release states debt to capitalization of 36% against the 33% maximum management set in the first quarter, so equity returns and buybacks draw on the same cushion that protects creditors; distributions of at least 90% of REIT taxable income are a requirement of the REIT regime and leave little retained cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A securities class action filed on October 9, 2026 adds an unquantified legal cost and a disclosure question. The complaint covers purchasers from February 7, 2025 to October 2, 2026 and claims under the Exchange Act, seeks unspecified damages, and Millrose says the claims have no merit; the management fee does not cover extraordinary litigation, so costs and any award fall on Millrose. The earlier source-readiness review did not record this event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is that the structure has performed: no property has been terminated, 93% of capital is pooled, the Lennar share of revenue fell from 84% in FY2025 to 69%, 22 counterparties now hold 76 pools, the debt-to-equity ratio of 0.57x is well inside Lennar's ceiling of one times equity, and the annual report schedules undiscounted option fees at December 31, 2025 that extend beyond 2030. Asset yield also exceeds funding cost: management states a 9.3% portfolio yield against an average coupon of 6.43% on USD 3,000 million of senior notes outstanding after October 6, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if counterparties outside Lennar were shown to carry guarantees comparable to Lennar's, if the August 2026 amendment removed none of the consent rights that limit leverage, and if the class action were dismissed. It would worsen on any pool-level termination by Lennar or by Dream Finders, a Lennar rating action if the rating-linked option pricing still applies, use of Lennar's consent rights to block financing, a sunset event that removes the leverage ceiling, or a move of the preferred instrument or rental homes into impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Millrose was created by Lennar's spin-off on February 7, 2025, which contributed about USD 5.5 billion of land assets and about USD 1.0 billion of cash that included USD 585 million of option deposit liabilities. Since then it has bought the Rausch homesites on February 10, 2025 for about USD 859 million net of deposits, funded USD 494.5 million at the June 25, 2025 closing of New Home's acquisition of Landsea, closed its first multifamily land banking acquisition with JPI on July 30, 2026, and supported Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes with funding of about USD 1.068 billion across September 14 and October 20, 2026. The FY2024 annual report gave about USD 876 million for the Rausch purchase, a difference logged in the conflict register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt came in four steps. The company issued USD 1.25 billion of senior notes due 2030 on August 7, 2025 and USD 750 million due 2032 on September 11, 2025, replaced its secured revolving facility with an unsecured credit agreement on March 25, 2026, signed a limited-recourse rental facility of up to USD 235 million on September 30, 2026, and closed USD 1.0 billion of senior notes due 2029 and 2031 on October 6, 2026. Amounts and ratios are in Financial foundation.

Countervailing evidence is the pooling, the Lennar guarantee and the leverage ceiling; further analysis requires the executed agreements and the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Millrose Properties, Inc. (issuer mrp-2017206) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the supplied filings and releases through the quarter ended September 30, 2026, read with the accepted analyses of source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance, in US dollars. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or position size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit is adequate but weakening: contractual option income covers interest comfortably today, yet debt has risen to 4.95x EBITDA and 36.33% of capitalization, above management's own 33% maximum target, while one builder group still supplies 69% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt to EBITDA of 4.85x becomes 6.18x pro forma for the Dream Finders funding of October 20, 2026, before any income those assets earn; the effect of the October 6, 2026 notes is not established. The contracts let Lennar pause for up to six months at half the option rate, which would cut last-twelve-months cover of senior note coupons from 3.50x to about 2.75x, before floating-rate interest. Creditors should treat the profile as adequate only while takedowns continue and leverage stops rising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C15; 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is contractual and well covered, but it depends on one builder group and on a contractual pause right. Option fees were 99.28% of third-quarter revenue, and the 2025 annual report schedules about USD 3.1 billion of undiscounted option fees on homesites then under contract. Lennar paid USD 144.9 million, 69% of the quarter's revenue, and may pause takedown and construction deadlines for up to six months in each of two periods, cutting its monthly option payments to half the applicable rate, if a local home price index falls 10% or more, in a public health emergency or at its own election. Its share has fallen from 84% in FY2025 as 21 other counterparties were added, and management says about 42% of the asset base is outside the Lennar program once the Dream Finders funding is counted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are not the weak point, but the cost base does not shrink when income does. Reported EBITDA margin was 85.18% over the last twelve months because the company has no employees and its main operating cost is a management fee of 1.25% of Tangible Assets, about USD 30.3 million or 14.34% of third-quarter revenue. The fee follows assets, not income, so a fall in option income would pass almost wholly to EBITDA, and interest is the larger fixed claim: third-quarter EBITDA covered accrued interest expense 3.83x, against 4.18x over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is a recycling of capital, and growth and distributions depend on borrowing. Takedowns of homesites were 85.86% of operating cash flow in the nine months to September 30, 2026. Without them operating cash flow was about USD 362 million, below dividends paid of about USD 379 million, so net borrowing of about USD 1.2 billion financed investment in new homesites and the distribution. The model recycles its own capital while takedowns continue; it does not generate free cash flow after distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage and coverage have deteriorated faster than the annual picture shows. Total debt to EBITDA rose from 3.83x at June 30, 2026 to 4.95x at September 30, 2026, and debt to capitalization of 36.33% is about USD 456 million of debt above management's 33% maximum target on the equity then reported. Net debt to EBITDA of 4.85x was 6.18x pro forma for the Dream Finders closing on October 20, 2026 and 5.04x pro forma for the dividend paid on October 15, 2026, each taken alone; the effect of the October 6, 2026 notes is not established. Cash interest cover of 4.66x is the first reading with a full year of coupons, and the annual coupons on the four senior note issues outstanding after October 6, 2026, about USD 193 million, are covered 3.50x by last-twelve-months EBITDA before any floating-rate interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 29, 40–41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months on contractual maturities, but it is thinner and its headroom is unverified. Cash plus undrawn committed facilities fell by about USD 545 million in the third quarter to about USD 0.8 billion, and only the revolving facility's USD 750 million is a working buffer, whose availability depends on a borrowing base the filings do not print, while the delayed draw term loan, almost fully drawn, can be drawn only until March 2027. Maturities before 2028 are small, but 70.51% of September 30, 2026 principal falls due in 2030, and covenant levels are not printed anywhere, so compliance is known only as reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy favors shareholders while leverage is above the stated target. Dividends paid were 99.94% of net income in the nine months, the quarterly dividend has risen to USD 0.79 a share, and on October 26, 2026 the board authorized repurchases of up to USD 250 million with none stated. The 33% maximum was stated in the first-quarter release and not restated in the later releases, so whether it still binds management is not established. The only contractual limit with a stated level is Lennar's ceiling of one times equity on debt, with debt to equity at 0.57x, and the August 27, 2026 amendment to Lennar's rights is not described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is moving into exposures that sit outside the pooled option protection. Funding for Dream Finders totals about USD 1.1 billion, of which a preferred instrument paying a 12% dividend is USD 487.5 million at purchase cost, and single-family rental homes bought from Lennar cost about USD 333 million. Management states a 10.8% yield on other agreements against 8.5% on the Lennar program, but the preferred instrument is a perpetual equity security of Dream Finders that ranks behind its debt and that Dream Finders may redeem from the third anniversary, its covenants are not described, rental income is not yet reported, and how much of the capital held with other counterparties is pooled is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 26, 41, 43, 45, 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance gives creditors little direct control, and a securities class action adds an unquantified cost. Class B stock held by the Miller Family carries about 43% of the votes, Lennar holds consent rights over the manager and over debt above one times equity, and the manager is paid on assets. A securities class action was filed on October 9, 2026 for purchasers from February 7, 2025 to October 2, 2026; the management fee does not cover extraordinary litigation, so any cost falls on Millrose, and management says the claims have no merit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is that the structure has performed. No option agreement has been terminated, forfeited or expired since inception, no counterparty delinquency has been recorded, the Lennar Corporation guarantee backs Lennar's payment obligations, and management reports that AFFO has risen for six consecutive quarters. Management states a portfolio yield of 9.3% against an average coupon of 6.43% on the senior notes outstanding after October 6, 2026, the portfolio's weighted average remaining life is 3.3 years against debt that is mostly due from 2030, and a quarterly income run rate of about USD 221 million is about USD 10 million above reported third-quarter revenue, so leverage could ease quickly if the new assets earn as stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if debt to capitalization returned to 33% or below without new equity because takedown proceeds repay the revolving facility instead of funding new commitments, if fourth-quarter revenue reached the run rate, if covenant levels proved to leave wide headroom, and if the class action were dismissed. It would worsen on any Lennar pause designation or pool-level termination, on a revolving draw that funds a distribution or a repurchase, on revenue below the run rate for a second quarter, or on evidence that the pricing grid or covenants bind at the current leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 25, 45, 47; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels, step-downs and borrowing bases are not printed, so the conclusion that liquidity is adequate could be wrong if headroom is narrow at debt to capitalization of 36.33%, and the loan pricing grid steps at two Leverage Ratio levels whose definition is not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Borrowings drawn and repaid after September 30, 2026 are not printed, so the pro forma leverage figures are isolated effects, and the conclusion that leverage keeps rising after the quarter could reverse if takedown proceeds repaid debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pause conditions are taken from the 2024 annual report, which names a fall of 10% or more in a local home price index, a public health emergency or Lennar's own election, while the 2025 annual report says only that they are subject to certain conditions, and the August 27, 2026 amendment to the Founder's Rights Agreement is not described, so whether Lennar's election is still unrestricted is not established and the weight given to Lennar concentration could be too high or too low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside figures apply the contractual half rate to Lennar's reported third-quarter revenue; the effect on revenue under lease accounting and on cash timing is not established, so the cover and leverage figures under a pause are sensitivities, not forecasts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filing gives the pooled share of invested capital as one figure and does not separate how much of the capital held under other agreements is pooled, so the conclusion that cross-termination protection extends beyond the Lennar program is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial foundation states that no material litigation is reported; that rests on the contingencies note at September 30, 2026 and omits the securities class action filed on October 9, 2026 and disclosed in the same report, so its statement on claims outside debt is incomplete by an unquantified legal exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contractual, pooled option income is the main credit support. Option fees were 99.28% of third-quarter revenue and are paid monthly on invested capital under agreements in which deposits are forfeited on non-exercise and options cross-terminate within a pool, and no option has been terminated since inception, so the cash that services debt has been predictable. The support is a design and a short record, not a tested downturn outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cost base is thin, so income converts to cover. Reported EBITDA margin was 85.18% over the last twelve months because there are no employees and the manager is paid 1.25% of Tangible Assets, so each dollar of option income reaches interest cover with little leakage, although the fee follows assets and does not fall when income does.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The funding stack is long and mostly unsecured, so refinancing risk is back-ended. About 92.71% of contractual principal at September 30, 2026 is unsecured, the senior notes carry fixed coupons, maturities before 2028 are only the purchase money mortgages, and the first large maturity is the rental facility in 2028, followed by the revolving and delayed draw facilities and the 2030 notes in 2030. That leaves little to refinance while takedowns continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 33–34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Counterparty diversification is improving. Lennar's share of revenue fell from 84% in FY2025 to 69% in the third quarter as capital held under other agreements rose to 36.46% of invested capital, which lowers dependence on a single payer and earns a higher stated yield of 10.8%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Builder deposits and takedown proceeds fund part of growth without new debt. Builder deposits were about USD 1.0 billion at September 30, 2026, up from December 31, 2025, and takedown proceeds were about USD 0.8 billion in the third quarter, so a share of new investment does not call on lenders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is above target and rising. Total debt to EBITDA of 4.95x and debt to capitalization of 36.33% follow a quarter in which debt grew by about USD 0.9 billion before the funded assets earned EBITDA, and net leverage of 6.18x pro forma for the Dream Finders closing on October 20, 2026 would be higher still, so the cushion for a revenue shock is smaller than at June 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One builder group and its pause right drive the income. Lennar paid 69% of third-quarter revenue and may pause for up to six months at half the option rate, so a market shock can cut income without any default, while pooled protection and the parent guarantee address default rather than a pause.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy leaves no retained cushion. Dividends were 99.94% of nine-month net income and a repurchase of up to USD 250 million is authorized while debt to capitalization exceeds the stated target, so equity returns compete with creditors for the same cash and growth is funded by borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is thinner and its true headroom is unverified. Cash plus undrawn committed facilities fell to about USD 0.8 billion in a quarter, availability depends on borrowing bases that are not printed, and the covenants that would show headroom are named without levels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33–34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and exposure outside the pools weaken creditor control. An external manager paid on assets, Lennar and Miller Family control rights, a preferred instrument in one builder, rental homes with no earnings record and a securities class action all sit beside debt that ranks ahead of the preferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Millrose is a residential land bank organised as a real estate investment trust. It buys and develops land, then gives homebuilders exclusive options to buy finished homesites at set prices on set takedown schedules, and earns monthly option fees on the capital it has invested; it operates in the United States only, in one reportable segment, and was spun off by Lennar on February 7, 2025. Cash flow is therefore a contractual yield on invested capital plus the return of that capital as homesites are taken down, which supports visibility of debt service while the options are performed, and which makes liquidity depend on takedown timing, not on sales of homes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Class A stock is publicly listed, Class B stock held by the Miller Family carries about 43% of the votes, Lennar holds a de minimis stake since November 28, 2025 but retains Founder's Rights, and Kennedy Lewis runs the company as external manager under a management agreement. The senior notes and credit facilities are guaranteed by two subsidiaries, and the notes are structurally subordinated to the debt of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them, while the rental facility and the purchase money mortgages sit at property-level borrowers with their own collateral. For creditors this means control sits with parties whose interests are not those of lenders, while the guarantors and the unsecured structure put the notes and bank facilities on the same rank.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ck0002017206-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 34–35, 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 29, 33–34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is the product of invested capital and a weighted yield, so it grows with funded capital, not with home prices or volumes. Capital invested reached USD 9,245.4 million at September 30, 2026 at a weighted yield of 9.3%, and takedown proceeds of USD 813.681 million in the quarter compare with USD 1,260.082 million of new funding. Pricing power is limited: the 2024 annual report fixed the rate on the assets transferred at spin-off at 8.5%, set the rate on Lennar's future assets from a three-year BBB index plus 4.00% and a rating adjustment tied to Lennar's credit rating, bounded between 7.0% and 10.0%, and gives Lennar the right to match any lower rate Millrose accepts from another counterparty. The 2025 annual report no longer prints the rating adjustment, so whether it still applies is not established. Other counterparties pay a higher stated yield of 10.8%, and contracted option fees of about USD 3.1 billion at the 2025 year end, excluding new homesites, give visibility of several years of income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating costs are mainly the management fee of 1.25% of Tangible Assets, USD 30.264 million in the third quarter, with stock-based compensation and credit-loss provisions small beside it, which gave an income-from-operations margin of 85.52% in the quarter. The fee follows assets, so margin holds while income grows with assets but falls quickly when income stops growing, because the fee does not fall with a pause, and extraordinary litigation and rating agency fees are borne outside the fee. Interest expense of USD 47.093 million in the quarter is the larger fixed claim and absorbs 26.10% of third-quarter income from operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company reports no maintenance or growth capital expenditure; land and development spending is investment in homesites under option, USD 3,150.232 million in the nine months, against takedown proceeds that return capital. Earnings convert to cash well, with operating cash flow excluding takedowns of USD 361.638 million against net income of USD 378.767 million, although development loan income, 0.72% of third-quarter revenue, is paid in kind. Dividends of USD 378.522 million take more than all of it, and the investment programme is financed by net borrowing. Capex flexibility exists in that new funding is discretionary within agreed programmes, yet future land development commitments of USD 6.7 billion, about 73% of them to Lennar, are funded as development is carried out under the construction agreements, in which Millrose reimburses actual costs up to agreed budgets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is limited but real: the 2025 annual report describes a niche of a select number of private funds and asset managers, and warns of aggressive pricing and alternative structures, so the 9.3% yield could compress on new projects, which lowers cover. The threat of new entrants is moderated by operating complexity and long-term capital needs, which management calls high barriers, but entrants with capital could overcome them, which would hit the yield on the 36.46% of capital held under other agreements first. Substitutes include traditional land banking arrangements and other providers, which the 2025 annual report says Lennar may choose instead, and the move of builders to an asset-light model supports demand. Buyer power is the central force: Lennar can match any lower rate offered to others, can pause at its own election under the 2024 terms, and supplies 69% of revenue, which limits pricing and weighs on recovery of income in a downturn. Supplier power is limited: development is performed by the counterparties, who bear cost overruns under the construction agreements, so input-cost inflation falls mainly on them, the manager's fee is set by contract, and land sellers are not described as a constraint in the documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two factors are material. Housing demand and mortgage affordability set builders' appetite to exercise options, so a fall of 10% or more in a local home price index is one stated trigger for pauses; management itself describes a challenging housing market. Interest rates matter twice: USD 1.345 billion of variable-rate borrowings means a one percentage point rise adds about USD 13.5 million of annual interest expense, 2.00% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, with no hedges, while part of the asset yield is stated at a prior SOFR level and how much of it reprices is not established. REIT status is a regulatory condition of the credit agreement and drives the distribution policy, so loss of status would be an event of concern; none is reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support credit are contractual option income, pooled cross-termination and deposit forfeiture, a thin cost base, a long and mostly unsecured maturity profile and rising counterparty diversification. Weaknesses that constrain it are debt above the stated target, dependence on Lennar and its pause right, a payout near net income, thin and unverified liquidity headroom and control held by an external manager, Lennar and the Miller Family.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C11; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the portfolio's weighted average remaining life of 3.3 years, which returns capital faster than debt falls due; asset yield of 9.3% against an average senior note coupon of 6.43%; a run rate above reported revenue; and a repurchase that stays unused. Threats that could weaken it are a Lennar pause or option termination, builder consolidation that shifts pricing, a rise in floating rates on USD 1.345 billion of borrowings, a covenant that binds at current leverage and adverse litigation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 29, 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale is meaningful, with reported EBITDA of about USD 675 million over twelve months, but the operating history is under two years and one counterparty group dominates, so market position is average rather than proven. Business diversification is weak by counterparty although improving, and about 53% of property assets sit in California, Florida and Texas, while 22 counterparties and 76 pools give some spread. The cost structure supports margin stability, but it is untested on income and cost flexibility is limited because the fee follows assets. Free cash flow after distributions is negative and is funded by borrowing, so its stability is weak. The ability to refinance looks adequate on evidence of senior note issues in August 2025, September 2025 and October 2026 at coupons of 6.25% to 6.75% and long maturities, but no rating is supplied. Liquidity is adequate but falling, and financial policy and governance are weak for creditors, because an external manager, concentrated control and a near-total payout sit with leverage above target.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 46–47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are contractual income, pooled protection and the long unsecured maturity profile. The main constraints are leverage above the stated target, concentration and the unverified covenant headroom. The trend is toward more debt and more exposure outside the pools. The key missing data are covenant levels, borrowing bases, borrowings after September 30, 2026, the preferred instrument's ranking and covenants and any rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 31, 40–41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are set out in Financial foundation and are not repeated in the ratios: USD 13 million of seller notes in other liabilities, a development guarantee holdback liability of USD 100 million, builder deposits of about USD 1.0 billion that are credited against takedown prices, and future land development commitments of USD 6.7 billion, with no pension, lease liability, factoring or supply-chain finance found. The securities class action filed on October 9, 2026 is a further claim, unquantified, that Financial foundation did not record.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 28–29, 34, 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the income run rate of about USD 221 million a quarter is about USD 10 million above third-quarter revenue and management raised its year-end AFFO outlook, which supports cover as the Dream Finders and rental assets begin to earn. Against that, the full coupons of the 2029 and 2031 notes add USD 66.25 million a year of interest, the dividend of about USD 131 million was paid on October 15, 2026, and leverage depends on takedown proceeds repaying the revolving facility. Over three to five years the portfolio's weighted average remaining life of 3.3 years and weighted average maturity of 53 months fall before the 2030 maturities of 70.51% of September 30, 2026 principal, so refinancing is likely to be met from the recycling of capital if new funding continues; a stall in takedowns would turn that into a market refinancing. Sector tailwinds are builders' shift to an asset-light model and consolidation that creates funding demand; headwinds are a challenging housing market and affordability. Company-specific tailwinds are the yield spread and diversification; headwinds are leverage, concentration and distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C22; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ck0002017206-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ck0002017206-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 40, 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a housing downturn, although none is needed: the 2024 annual report lets Lennar designate two pause periods of up to six months each on a property if a local home price index falls 10% or more or in a public health emergency, and also at its own election under its Founder's Rights, and similar provisions in other counterparty agreements could delay takedowns and cut cash inflows. In the first operational break Lennar, which paid USD 144.9 million in the third quarter, pauses takedown and construction deadlines and pays half the applicable monthly option rate: in this illustration that removes USD 72.45 million of option income a quarter, 34.34% of third-quarter revenue and 40.15% of third-quarter EBITDA, while takedown proceeds that repay the revolving facility are delayed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission is fast because costs are tied to assets and debt: the management fee follows assets, senior note coupons are fixed, and distributions continue at about 100% of net income. Over a six-month pause last-twelve-months EBITDA falls by USD 144.9 million to about USD 530 million, total debt to EBITDA on the September 30, 2026 balance sheet rises from 4.95x to 6.30x, net debt to EBITDA pro forma for the Dream Finders closing rises from 6.18x to 7.87x, and cover of senior note coupons falls from 3.50x to about 2.75x before floating-rate interest. If both permitted periods were used, the reduction would be USD 289.8 million, leverage 8.67x and coupon cover 2.00x, and the agreements allow two further periods by mutual agreement, up to two years in total, which would need Millrose's consent. These are sensitivities on contract terms and reported figures, not forecasts, and the effect on revenue under lease accounting is not established.

fields.value: On liquidity, cash plus undrawn committed facilities of about USD 0.8 billion at September 30, 2026 faces a dividend of about USD 131 million a quarter, funding commitments to builders under contracts for USD 6.7 billion of future development, and a revolving facility whose borrowing base and covenants are not printed; the borrowing base would be the first constraint if collateral values fell. Maturities do not force a refinancing before 2028, so a pause tests covenants and market access before it tests repayment. Management levers are to leave the USD 250 million repurchase unused, to hold the dividend near the minimum REIT distribution, to slow discretionary new funding, to repay revolving borrowings from takedowns by other counterparties and to sell land. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress inside twelve months on contractual maturities, and insufficient to protect the 33% maximum target, because debt to capitalization is already 36.33%. The observable triggers are a pause notice, a fall in the monthly option payments received, takedown proceeds below the third-quarter level, a revolving draw that funds a distribution and any covenant disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Millrose presents an adequate business profile supported by contractual option income, pooled protection, an 85.18% EBITDA margin and a long, mostly unsecured maturity profile, but credit quality is constrained by debt of 36.33% of capitalization above the 33% maximum target, concentration in Lennar and a distribution policy that leaves growth funded by borrowing. Cash-flow durability appears adequate while takedowns continue, because option fees were 99.28% of revenue and are contractual, but it is untested in a pause. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued takedown proceeds, on market acceptance of the 6.50% and 6.75% coupons paid on the 2029 and 2031 notes and on borrowing bases that are not printed. The primary downside path is a Lennar pause or builder slowdown that delays takedowns while distributions and committed funding continue, which would lift leverage to about 6.30x total debt to EBITDA on the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Further analysis would require covenant levels, borrowing bases, ratings, the preferred instrument's ranking and covenants and borrowings after September 30, 2026. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: a Lennar pause or takedown slowdown while leverage is above the stated target.
